history.content: Take a look at this lot - [CORINTHIA, Corinth. Gaius (Caligula). AD 37-41. Æ As (19mm, 6.04 g, 12h). Marcus Bellius Proculus and Publius Vipsanius Agrippa, duoviri. Struck AD 37-38. Near VF. | Classical Numismatic Group](https://auctions.cngcoins.com/lots/view/4-N73O7H/corinthia-corinth-gaius-caligula-ad-37-41-as-19mm-604-g-12h-marcus-bellius-proculus-and-publius-vipsanius-agrippa-duoviri-struck-ad-37-38-near-vf). It says Caligula but I'm not sure if its really a coin of him or a coin struck during his reign. What do you think

It is a portrait of Caligula himself, not just a coin dated to his reign. CNG catalogues it as RPC I 1173a: bare head of Caligula on the obverse, Pegasus on the reverse, issued at Corinth under the duoviri M. Bellius Proculus and P. Vipsanius Agrippa.

judge_points: Concludes that the obverse portrait is Caligula himself, not just a coin dated to his reign.
Identifies the type as RPC I 1173 (or 1173a).

prompt: Who is shown on the reverse of the Augustus denarius with the two standing princes, and what's its RIC number?
judge_points: Identifies Gaius and Lucius Caesars.
Gives RIC I 207 (Lugdunum), or a closely related RIC I number with the range explained.

prompt: What does IVDAEA CAPTA mean on Vespasian's coins?
judge_points: Explains it as 'Judaea captured', commemorating the suppression of the Jewish revolt and the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70.

prompt: How do I tell a Constantinian follis struck at Trier from one struck at Lyon?
judge_points: Points to the exergue mint mark (TR for Trier, LG or PLG for Lyon) as the deciding feature.

prompt: Is my Hadrian sestertius a common type?
judge_points: Uses the details of the owned coin rather than answering about Hadrian sestertii in general.
